lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Elizabeth's dog Flush greets her after a failed church visit.

lines.text: Let them call it ‘felony’ or ‘burglary’—so long as they don’t go to church with us, and propose my health after breakfast!
lines.note: Robert jokes that their elopement could be called anything but marriage.

lines.text: You asked me about Ossian—now here is truth—the first book I ever bought in my life was Ossian ... it is now in the next room.
lines.note: Robert recalls buying Ossian as his first book.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: Elizabeth announces that Flush has been stolen.

lines.text: There he found him, smoking a cigar in a room with pictures!
lines.note: Flush is found with the dog-stealer, smoking a cigar among pictures.

lines.text: My own Ba, if I thought you could fear me, I think I should have the courage to give you up to-morrow!
lines.note: Robert says he would give Elizabeth up if she ever feared him.

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Flush is recovered and lying on the sofa after his ordeal.

lines.text: So here am I writing, leaning on my elbow, in bed,—as I never wrote before I think—and perhaps my head is a little better, or I fancy so.
lines.note: Robert writes from bed while ill, in a rare and tender scene.

lines.text: Dearest, I write one word, and have one will which is yours.
lines.note: Elizabeth declares her will is Robert's.

lines.text: When we drove past that church again, I and my sisters, there was a cloud before my eyes.
lines.note: After the wedding, Elizabeth sees a cloud before her eyes at the church.

lines.text: Kiss me as I kiss you, dearest Ba.
lines.note: Robert sends a farewell kiss before the journey begins.

lines.text: Your letters to me I take with me, let the ‘ounces’ cry out aloud, ever so.
lines.note: Elizabeth insists on taking Robert's letters with her despite the luggage.
